title: Windows installer lacks compatibility and pre-mutation regression coverage
reasoning: The POSIX tests verify rejection of mismatched ClawPatch and ClawHub versions and prove that unsupported Python is rejected before the installation directory is created. The complete Windows test section covers dependency presence, missing npm, and npm failures, but has no equivalent version-mismatch or unsupported-Python cases. A Windows installer regression that accepts protocol-incompatible dependencies or mutates the installation before validating Python could therefore pass the suite and ship.
recommendation: Extend the Windows installer harness so command stubs return configurable ClawPatch and ClawHub versions and the Python stub can fail the minimum-version probe. Add Windows tests asserting rejection, diagnostic text, and absence of the installation root for both dependency-version mismatches and Python older than 3.11.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The Windows helper does not accept dependency-version parameters or a Python-version failure mode, and every Windows test in the file exercises only presence, absence, or npm installation failure.
minimumFixScope: tests/test_installers.py only: enhance _run_windows_installer and its stubs, then add the three missing contract tests.
